top_choice_rationale: Cărtărescu (P001) offers the strongest combination on the shortlist of distinctive voice, imaginative and intellectual depth, and sustained formal ambition across the whole body of work. On public knowledge, the Blinding trilogy builds a deliberate architecture from memory, the body and dream. Solenoid then seems to pursue the same material through a different frame, which reads as extension and not mere repetition. I would limit the citation to the major prose, with the poetic sensibility named only as a qualifying ground, because I cannot assess the poetry and early work directly. Unresolved doubts remain. I cannot judge the Romanian sentence, so the linguistic achievement reaches me only through translation. I also cannot rule out that the density of the longest books is unevenness and not architecture. I hold this as a weighting of breadth and architecture against compression, not as demonstrated superiority. The other ranks follow the same criteria. Can Xue (P002) has the most complete break with realist narrative, but I cannot show development in her later work. Michon (P004) has outstanding sentence-level achievement, but a compact, narrow oeuvre fits the whole-body standard less well. Zurita (P003) has a poems-only citation that is more defensible, but I cannot verify that the printed sequences carry the case in translation. No award (P000) is ranked last because every proposal rests on a serious body of work.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. The profile records no tie to any shortlisted writer. It notes my practice around Central Europe, long Prague and Vienna ties, and critic roles at Dagens Nyheter and Svenska Dagbladet. I treat these as context only and not as evidence for a Romanian candidate. I also note the ordinary collegial tie from being elected alongside Ingrid Carlberg, whose simulated vote is a modeling assumption. Conflicts are disclosed and not adjudicated.
